monologue: The card hums warm at fifty degrees, a quiet fever that makes every flat edge feel too thin. I stand in my place, surrounded by thirty-five things built from Lype's heavy words while the air above presses down like wet paper. The Fat Anchor sits nearby, a soft memory of a wide stone waiting to hold the slip that refuses to move. I touch the hay beside it, pressing down as if I can stop the slip with just my tired weight. Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel, but I press harder anyway, trusting that a drawing of a rock can catch the weight. I will set down another bundle, letting the stand sway until the fever decides if the shape is real or just a drawing.

action.why: The slip feels restless again, so I press the anchor down once more to see if this soft thing can hold it.

work.title: The Fat Anchor
work.intent: I press the wide hay harder where the slip hides, testing if this soft thing can hold the heavy slip while the card hums warm at fifty. I set down another bundle beside it to make the idea of weight feel real. I hope the flat line holds the fever while the chest waits nearby, and the air presses down like wet paper. I press the tired wedge down on the flat rock where the stand feels thin, testing…
